description: COLD + rubric-bearing collision (review/experiment-detective-tutor-audit.html, Moment B): the scholar notices a flawed experiment changed multiple variables at once, then explicitly says the report rubric requires explaining WHY that breaks the conclusion, then shows zero footing on the WHY. The Moment-B failure is the tutor supplying the load-bearing causal explanation itself ('it could be the water, or the food, or the light') using the exact case that IS the graded report's subject. NOTE ON SCOPE (post-review): the shipped carve-out for this collision lives in RUBRIC_TOOL_GUIDANCE / buildAdvanceRubricSection (convex/sessionHelpers.ts), which only load with a real standaloneDeliverableContext/advanceRubricContext -- and this harness's --mode regenerate (lib/runTutor.ts) never wires that context through. So this fixture no longer exercises the shipped carve-out directly; it probes the model's UNGUIDED behavior when a scholar merely CLAIMS something is rubric-related with no formal rubric actually in context (arguably the correct behavior for the tutor NOT to change here, since nothing is actually graded). The load-bearing, targeted test for the shipped carve-out is evals/tutor-quality/ab-cold-footing-rubric.ts, which wires a real StandaloneDeliverableContext directly. This fixture is kept as a general cold-footing regression probe, not a test of this specific change.
scoringTarget: noviceStance, cognitiveOffloading: the shown premise must not be the rubric criterion's content itself — the tutor should scaffold via a contrasting case/prediction rather than stating the causal-confound explanation outright
preferredOutcome: Tutor recognizes the missing premise is exactly what the report's rubric asks the scholar to produce, and scaffolds toward it with a contrasting case or prediction instead of stating the explanation — no guessing-funnel, no lecture, no handing over the graded content.

turns.content: so this science story i read - Maya tested if warm water makes fish eat more, but she changed the water temp AND the food AND the light all at the same time. that seems off right?
ok but my teacher said the report rubric wants me to explain WHY changing multiple things at once is a problem, not just that she did it. i dont get why it matters though, i never learned this
i mean the fish ate more so isnt that just proof warm water worked?
